essence: FlyVis is, mathematically, a convolutional recurrent network on a hexagonal lattice: 65 cell-type channels (R1-R8 photoreceptors, lamina, medulla, T4a-d/T5a-d, Tm/TmY; no lobula LC/LPLC), 605 type-to-type edge kernels whose taps are fixed hexagonal offsets (du, dv) taken from the connectome (synapse count x sign x one learned strength per edge type), plus one bias and one time constant per cell type (734 free parameters in total), with threshold-linear leaky-integrator dynamics advanced by explicit Euler (dv/dt = (-v + bias + sum w*ReLU(v_src) + input)/max(tau, dt)). Because every parameter is shared across columns, the 721-column eye can be re-implemented densely over a whole 960x540 frame as a stack of small depthwise convolutions in axial hex coordinates (HexaConv/HexagDLy idea), with the connectome's own taps as fixed masks. The crucial design choice is spatial scale: FlyVis was trained with one column per 13x13-pixel box on Sintel, and the project's tiled mode (column step about 13.3 px) already matches that scale; densifying should therefore keep the 13-px column spacing and fill the frame with many phase-shifted lattices (polyphase / dilated formulation, equivalent to a dense per-pixel map with taps dilated by the column spacing), not put one column per pixel (that changes the apparent scale 13x, outside the documented range-limited scale stability). Our own micro-benchmark of such a dense implementation on the project's RTX 5070 gives 15.8 ms per Euler step at full per-pixel density (518,400 columns, fp16, no gradient), i.e. about 32 ms per 30 Hz frame with 2 steps, and 1.2 ms per step at 1/16 density. Published uses of FlyVis or connectome-constrained networks in computer vision exist (fly-following in NeuroMechFly v2, frozen FlyVis descriptors on architectural drawings, a drone-detection adapter repository, a larval-connectome classifier), but none is a full-frame dense deployment feeding a modern detector, and the most careful ones find that the circuit does not beat its own retina/input under matched controls - the same pattern the project already measured.

fly_role: Role recommended: a frozen (later lightly fine-tuned) full-frame evidence map used to RE-SCORE low-confidence candidates (conf 0.01-0.25) and, only if that passes, as an extra zero-initialised input branch/adapter of YOLO26 at the P3 (stride 8) level. Concretely: (1) Front end: the project's retina/lamina stage (tracking/retina.py, Naka-Rushton photoreceptor + lamina contrast normalisation), which already removes the fly's night failure, feeds R1-R8 of the dense fly. (2) Dense fly: all 65 types computed on a polyphase hex lattice with the trained column spacing (about 13 px, box-filter 13x13 receptive field, the same scale as tiled mode), with P phase shifts (each phase is about 74 x 48 = 3,550 columns over 960x540; P = 9, i.e. 3 x 3 sub-column shifts, gives about 32,000 columns and an effective sampling step of about 4.4 x 3.8 px; P = 146 gives one column centre per pixel, 518,400 columns). Implementation: each phase is an axial-coordinate rectangular buffer; the 605 edge kernels become depthwise convolutions with fixed hex masks taken from the connectome (bucketed by radius: 212 edges 1x1, 223 radius 1, 103 radius 2, 33 radius 3, 25 radius 4, 9 radius 5-6 in axial square extent; 2,378 taps per column after flyvis's convex-hull fill), followed by index_add into the 65 target channels; exact equivalence with flyvis's sparse scatter implementation can be unit-tested on a single 721-column phase against Network.simulate (same dt, same params). (3) What is read out, and why: not T4/T5 alone (tiled T4/T5 readout was indistinguishable from shuffled and worse than the decoded flow for q_match), but (a) small-field, size-tuned channels T2, T2a, T3 and Tm/TmY (the inputs of LC11, the fly's small-object detector, which FlyVis lacks downstream), (b) local motion contrast: T4/T5 inside the box minus a surround ring (figure-ground that the missing lobula would compute; needed because a forward-moving car camera drives T4/T5 everywhere), (c) ON/OFF transient energy (L1/L2-Mi1/Tm3 path), which is the only fly signal that carries information at a target's first frame (age 0) when the detector has no temporal context. Why it is meaningful at all: the fly integrates 30 Hz frames recurrently (time constants tens of ms, 2 Euler steps per frame), i.e. it gives each candidate a short temporal history the per-frame YOLO26 does not have; the threshold loss (candidate present but under-confident, 21.0% night vs 15.5% day) is exactly where a second, temporally integrated opinion can help. Why not a dense per-pixel lattice at 1 px per column: it changes the apparent scale 13x relative to training (motion of several px per frame becomes many columns per step, aliasing the 1-column correlator of T4/T5) and is outside the scale range where FlyVis direction codes transfer (Dhiman and Panwar 2026). A second, finer scale (column step about 6.5 px) for small boxes is an option only after checking the fly's response at that scale on our own stimuli. (4) Modification freedom: since the user allows unlimited modification, the dense implementation can add an LC11-like learned readout (T2/T3 -> small 3x3 hex convolution -> size-tuned ReLU) or train the 734 parameters end to end; both must be compared against a parameter-matched non-connectome recurrent network and a shuffled connectome.
loss_mechanism_targeted: Primary: THRESHOLD loss. 21.0% of night objects (15.5% day) have a candidate that is under-confident (night by +0.098); 2/3 of the age-0 gap (31% found at age 0 at night vs 68% at age 10+) also goes through the threshold. A dense map that adds temporally integrated, retina-adapted evidence at the candidate location is a direct attack on this: the candidate box already exists (cache at conf 0.01), only its score is wrong. Secondary: small objects (56.7% found) - only through T2/T3/Tm size-tuned channels and only for objects at least about half a column (about 6-7 px) in size; below that the 13x13 box filter dilutes contrast to under 25% and dense phase sampling does not improve acuity. Occlusion at night (5.4x penalty) - plausible via recurrent persistence of activity when an object is partially hidden, but no evidence; low priority. Over-exposure - addressed by the photoreceptor adaptation front end, not by the connectome itself (the project's DIS control showed the gain from the retina is fly-specific, but the Kuklev 2026 result suggests the retina, not the circuit, may carry it). NOT targeted: BLINDNESS (4.5%, equal day and night) - a re-scoring signal cannot create a candidate that does not exist; as an input branch the fly could in principle create candidates, but the night deficit is not in this stage, so this would be optimising the wrong stage (the same arithmetic that closed the NoManNight phases).
novelty_overlap: Already done: (1) FlyVis applied outside neuroscience: NeuroMechFly v2 (Nature Methods 2024) drives FlyVis with rendered fly-eye input and puts a hexagonal CNN on top for fly following (object direction/distance/size) - a tracking-like use, in simulation. (2) Kuklev, arXiv 2609.24565 (Sept 2026): frozen FlyVis driven by prescribed drift over document patches as a descriptor, with degree-preserving and type-preserving rewiring nulls (wiring is load-bearing: 0.857 vs 0.539) and matched baselines; key negative: the circuit does not beat the moving retina in front of it (receptors-only 0.891-0.894 vs circuit 0.835-0.857; circuit + conv decoder 0.962 AP vs receptors + same decoder 0.961). (3) FlyVision Adapter repository: a FlyVis 'connectome-constrained adapter' for small drone detection with a shuffled-connectome control - the closest concept to 'fly as detector adapter', but no results published as of 03.10.2026; it must be cited and re-checked before submission. (4) Dhiman 2026: FlyVis-graph topology advantages vanish under degree-preserving nulls and shared initialisation. (5) Dhiman and Panwar 2026: FlyVis direction codes are stable only within a range of apparent scales. (6) Hexagonal convolutions in axial coordinates (HexaConv 2018, HexagDLy 2019) - the dense re-implementation technique itself is not new. (7) Connectome-as-architecture classifiers (BPU 2025 on the larval connectome; Elegans-AI 2024) - connectome networks as general vision models, MNIST/CIFAR level. (8) Dense recurrent state over the whole frame inside a real-time detector is standard (RVT, CVPR 2023). Implication for cannot_claim: cannot claim the first use of FlyVis/connectome networks in computer vision, the first hexagonal or convolutional re-implementation, or that connectome topology per se improves detection (the project's own fly_connectome_null_v1 shows +0.044 AP real vs shuffled for the fly's own representation but only +0.0032 [-0.0028; +0.0100] once input features are present). What may still be claimable, if the gate passes: a full-frame polyphase deployment of a pretrained connectome-constrained fly model at its trained scale as candidate-level evidence for a modern NMS-free detector (YOLO26) on real moving-camera video, with same-input (retina only), shuffled-connectome and parameter-matched controls, analysed by loss mechanism (threshold vs blindness). Doubt about novelty is noted and does not stop the work (the FlyVision Adapter repository may publish first).
author_results: Lappalainen et al. 2024: 45,669 neurons, 1,513,231 connections, 64 (65 with CT1 compartments) cell types, 721 columns (31 across), 734 free parameters (65 resting potentials, 65 time constants, 604 synapse-strength scale factors); trained on Sintel optic flow (frames 1,024 x 436, photoreceptors 13 px apart, each the mean of a 13 x 13 box; 24 fps resampled to 50 Hz), Euler integration, dt < 20 ms reported better, 50-model ensemble, 250,000 iterations, batch 4; validation is neural (predicts direction selectivity of T4/T5 and other cells), not a vision benchmark; no detection numbers. NeuroMechFly v2: demonstrates successful fly following in simulation with FlyVis + hexagonal CNN; no comparison to a modern detector [uncertain: numeric following accuracy not extracted]. Kuklev 2026 (architectural drawings, not video, static camera with prescribed drift): frozen FlyVis hatch matching 0.857 area-weighted accuracy vs task-trained CNN 0.959 (dev); held-out test 0.835 vs receptors-only 0.894 vs task-trained 0.971-0.980; wall segmentation IoU 0.619 vs matched CNN 0.905; on a closed 14-sheet production set the frozen fly (1,876 trainable params) reached 0.505 AP vs a 365,921-param CNN 0.415 (single small set, opened once); replacing motion by a static frame costs 0.089 accuracy; T4/T5 knockout changes hatch by +0.015 and segmentation by -0.076 IoU; frozen-circuit training 7,622 s vs CNN 166 s and 778 MiB vs 28 MiB. Dhiman 2026: under weak controls connectome loss 0.514 vs random 0.698; under shared initialisation + degree-preserving nulls loss difference +0.0003 (negligible). Dhiman and Panwar 2026: leave-one-scale-out direction decoding 0.885 across 8 apparent scales, 0.986 on the 6 interior scales, chance (0.167) at the upper boundary; after T4/T5 silencing a refitted decoder keeps 0.891 while the fixed decoder drops to 0.193 [uncertain: exact scale values not extracted]. BPU 2025: MNIST 98% vs size-matched MLP 97%, CIFAR-10 58% (weak baselines). RVT 2023 (event cameras, not RGB): Gen1 47.2 mAP, under 12 ms on a T4 GPU - shows a dense recurrent full-frame state is affordable inside a detector. Project measurements relevant to this item: tiled FlyVis in the tracker (flyvis_stress) HOTA 29.11 vs ByteTrack 52.44 although DetA 54.41 vs 52.81, pipeline 17.37 fps; tiled T4/T5 readout for q_match AP 0.943199 vs base+DIS 0.945423 (CI entirely negative), indistinguishable from shuffled; foveal readout beats shuffled (+0.002093, CI [+0.001009; +0.003450]) but not the base; HGB nonlinear readout: no FlyVis variant above base (0.9660-0.9671 vs 0.967989); q_birth tiled readout ΔAP -0.0004 [-0.0014; +0.0007]. Own micro-benchmark (dense depthwise re-implementation, real taps, RTX 5070): fp16 no-grad 1.2 ms/step at 135x240 (1/16 density), 3.6 ms/step at 270x480 (1/4), 15.8 ms/step at 540x960 (full per-pixel, 518,400 columns); fp32 28.5 ms/step at full density; with gradients, peak memory 0.33 GiB for 4 steps at 1/16 density, 5.04 GiB for 16 steps (8 frames x 2 steps) at 1/4 density, 2.72 GiB for 2 steps at full density (about 1.36 GiB per step, so full-density BPTT over 8 frames would need about 22 GiB without checkpointing).
strong_baseline_check: No published work tests FlyVis or any connectome-constrained network against a modern detector (YOLO/DETR family) at equal training budget; the only matched-control evidence points the other way: Kuklev 2026 finds that the intact circuit does not beat the receptor (retina) input under the same decoder (0.962 vs 0.961 AP; 0.835 vs 0.894 accuracy), Dhiman 2026 finds topology advantages vanish under degree-preserving nulls, and the project's own controls agree (dis_retina_control_v1: the retina helps the fly but not DIS; fly_connectome_null_v1: real vs shuffled +0.0032 with CI through zero once input features are present; tiled and foveal readouts not above base + DIS, also with a nonlinear HGB readout). No independent reproductions of a detection gain exist. Therefore any gate here must include: (a) same-input control - the retina/lamina output pooled over the same box and ring and over the same temporal window (frame differences of the adapted image), with no connectome; (b) shuffled-connectome and degree-preserving-rewired fly at the same dense scale; (c) parameter-matched generic ConvGRU/leaky-integrator network on the same lattice with the same 734-parameter budget (or the same trainable budget if fine-tuned); (d) the detector's own score and geometry as base, against which post-hoc rescoring has already failed (AUC 0.9025 -> 0.9005; q_det head AP 0.9190 -> 0.9197, CI [-0.016; +0.007]).
conditions_breakdown: None of the cited works reports night, over-exposure, occlusion, small-object or first-appearance breakdowns, and none uses BDD100K. Dhiman and Panwar 2026 is the only scale breakdown (apparent scale, synthetic stimuli). Project data provide the only night/day split for FlyVis: fly_connectome_null_v1 dark +0.0497 vs light +0.0391 for the fly's own representation, +0.0063 vs +0.0036 (dark CI through zero) with input features; the retina front end turns the dark-video fly contribution from -0.027 to +0.011 (flyvis_retina_frontend_v1).
cheap_gate: Gate G-D2 (a few GPU hours, no detector training), written before running. Step 0 (1 h, correctness): implement the dense polyphase fly; test equivalence with flyvis Network.simulate on one 721-column phase (max |Δactivity| < 1e-3 after fade-in on a val7 clip, same dt = 1/60, same checkpoint as tiled mode) and that P = 1 at 13.3 px spacing reproduces the existing tiled activity cache (runs/flyvis_activity) within the same tolerance. Step 1 (1-2 h GPU, inference only): run the frozen dense fly at P = 9 (about 32,000 columns, 1/16 of per-pixel density: 1.2 ms/step measured, 2 steps per frame, plus retina front end and video decoding; a few minutes per 30 Hz video) over the 7 val7 videos and over the dark test videos used by stage B, keeping 34 output types + T2/T2a/T3 maps at the labelled 5 Hz frames only (float16, box-pooled, not full maps, to keep disk small). Step 2 (CPU, 1 h): take candidates from runs/det_cache_ctl_960 (conf 0.01, imgsz 960, weights/baseline_seed42/best.pt) with 0.01 <= conf < 0.25 (the threshold-loss band), label each as TP (IoU >= 0.5 with an unmatched GT, class-aware) or FP; features per candidate: inside/ring pooling of T2/T2a/T3/Tm/TmY, T4/T5 motion contrast, ON/OFF transient energy, coverage. Ladder of logistic (and HGB) heads, train on 4 videos, test on 3 held-out (plus leave-one-video-out on the larger dark set): base = conf + class + box geometry + scene brightness (the closed post-hoc rescoring, AUC 0.9025 reference); + same-input control (retina/lamina only, same pooling, same temporal window); + dense fly; + shuffled fly; + parameter-matched random recurrent net. Pre-registered thresholds: (1) dense fly over base + same-input control: ΔAUC >= +0.010 on the low-confidence band, 95% video-bootstrap CI above zero, positive on every held-out video; (2) dense fly beats shuffled fly by >= +0.005 with CI above zero; (3) night not worse than day (ΔAUC_night >= ΔAUC_day - 0.002); (4) operational: at the detector's working threshold and a fixed FP count per frame, recovered night threshold losses >= 10% relative (i.e. the 21.0% night threshold loss falls to <= 18.9%) on held-out videos; (5) age-0 stratum reported separately (no threshold, descriptive). If (1) or (2) fails, the dense fly is closed for detection re-scoring by the same rule as A1 (the readout negative is not re-run with other pooling). Optional Step 3 (only if Step 2 passes, 2-3 h): same features at P = 146 (full density, 15.8 ms/step) and a second scale (column step about 6.5 px) restricted to boxes < 32 px, to see whether density or scale is limiting for small objects.
cost_here: Inference of the dense fly (measured, fp16, RTX 5070, no gradient, 2 Euler steps per 30 Hz frame): 1/16 density (P = 9, about 32,000 columns) 2.4 ms/frame, 1/4 density 7.2 ms/frame, full per-pixel density about 32 ms/frame (about 31 fps), plus the retina front end; for comparison YOLO26s is 20.9 GFLOPs at 640 (about 27 GFLOPs for 960x544), while the full-density fly is about 5 GMAC per step (9,717 multiply-adds per column with square-bucketed depthwise kernels; 2,378 with exact hex taps) but memory-bound. The stock flyvis sparse scatter implementation would need about 1.1 G edge operations per step at full density (1.51 M edges per 721 columns scaled to 518,400 columns) and is not the right tool [uncertain: not timed]. Gate G-D2: about 2-4 GPU hours total including fade-in and caching, no training. Full check as a detector branch: the fly needs a 30 Hz history while BDD100K MOT labels are 5 Hz, so each training sample requires running the fly over the preceding frames (e.g. 8 frames = 16 steps); with a frozen fly this can be precomputed once per video into a cache of a few channels at stride 8 (P3 resolution, 120 x 68 for 960x540; about 16 KB per channel per frame in fp16), so detector training cost stays close to the baseline: fine-tuning from best.pt with a zero-initialised adapter 12 epochs about 4.3-5 h (plus the observed DRB overhead risk, +17%), and the required 3 seeds x 12 epochs about 13-15 h, plus 100-epoch confirmation about 35 h per seed. Precomputing the cache over the 1,400 training videos at 30 Hz (about 1,200 frames each, about 1.7 M frames) at 1/16 density is about 1.7 M x (2.4 ms + IO) = about 1.5-3 h GPU [uncertain: IO and decoding of the zipped videos not measured]. Training the fly end to end (734 parameters + readout) at 1/4 density with 8-frame BPTT fits in about 5 GiB (measured 5.04 GiB) per sample, so batch 1-2 next to YOLO26s at 960 would not fit comfortably in 12 GB; requires gradient checkpointing or a separate stage - estimated 2-3x baseline training time [uncertain].
expected_effect: Honest prior: small. Evidence: post-hoc rescoring with class/geometry/scene did not move AUC (0.9025 -> 0.9005); the project's q_det head is flat (0.9190 -> 0.9197); every FlyVis readout so far was at most at the level of base + DIS (tiled -0.0024 AP, foveal -0.0004, HGB no gain); the topology advantage disappears once input features are present (+0.0032, CI through zero); Kuklev 2026 finds the circuit no better than its retina under matched decoders. What is new and could change the sign: (a) dense coverage removes the 'nearest column' fallback of tiled mode for small boxes, (b) evidence is used for detection candidates in the threshold band, where the detector has no temporal context, rather than for association where geometry already saturates (AP about 0.945), (c) the retina front end that removed the night failure is included. Plausible range if the gate passes: ΔAUC +0.005-0.015 in the 0.01-0.25 band [uncertain], recovering perhaps 5-15% of night threshold losses at fixed FP (night threshold loss 21.0% -> about 18-20%) [uncertain]; propagated to the tracker this is at most a few hundred of the 15,763 FN and DetA +0.1-0.4 [uncertain], nightly mAP50 change within or slightly above the control spread (0.3772 +/- 0.0031). As a trained input branch the expected gain is lower than as a re-scorer, because the detector already sees the same pixels (same-input argument) and the DRB experience shows small branches drown in 0.0144 seed noise.
risks: (1) Same-input trap: the gain may come from the retina/lamina adaptation or simple frame differencing, not from the connectome (Kuklev 2026; project dis_retina_control_v1) - the same-input control is mandatory and is the most likely winner. (2) Scale mismatch: column spacing at 1 px is outside the trained scale (range-limited scale stability; chance at the upper scale boundary), and objects smaller than about half a column (6-7 px) are invisible to the 13x13 box regardless of density. (3) Ego-motion: a forward-moving car camera saturates T4/T5 over the whole field; without a figure-ground stage (no LC/LPLC in FlyVis) the motion channels may only encode depth/position, which the detector's geometry already knows. (4) Implementation errors: hex-to-axial mapping, padding at lattice borders, Lawf1/Lawf2 strided types (stride 3,2) and the hull-filled offsets must reproduce flyvis exactly - unit test against Network.simulate before any metric. (5) DRB lessons: seed noise 0.0144 mAP at 12 epochs and a sign flip at 100 epochs mean no branch result is accepted without 3 seeds, a confidence interval and the 100-epoch check; a zero-initialised adapter can stay at zero (branch without gradient) - log the adapter's weight norm and gradient per epoch; the +17% time of DRB is comparable to the fly cache IO. (6) Temporal leakage: features must use only frames <= t (a causal recurrent net is causal by construction, but caching and interpolation must be checked as in flyvis_internal_readout_v1). (7) Non-comparable comparisons: the fly gate uses val7 / dark test videos only, while detector metrics are on full val; do not transfer the sign from 7 videos to full val. (8) Memory: full-density BPTT needs about 22 GiB for 8 frames; end-to-end training must use 1/4-1/16 density or checkpointing. (9) Licences: flyvis MIT (compatible); Ultralytics AGPL-3.0 (already accepted by the project); FlyVision Adapter repository has no visible licence - concept citation only, no code reuse. (10) Novelty: the FlyVision Adapter project may publish a fly-as-detector-adapter result first.
attribution: Borrowed: the FlyVis model, connectome (fib25-fib19 v2.2), dynamics and pretrained checkpoints (Lappalainen et al. 2024, MIT); axial-coordinate hexagonal convolution idea (Hoogeboom et al. 2018; Steppa and Holch 2019); YOLO26 detector (Ultralytics); the controls design (degree-preserving / shuffled connectome, matched baselines) follows Kuklev 2026 and Dhiman 2026. Ours: the dense polyphase re-implementation of FlyVis at its trained scale over a full 960x540 frame with equivalence tests; the retina/lamina front end; the use of dense fly evidence for re-scoring detection candidates in the threshold band and its gate with same-input and parameter-matched controls on BDD100K MOT; the loss-mechanism analysis (threshold vs blindness) that motivates it. Any negative outcome is reported as an investigated direction, not as a contribution.
